question.text: Assertion: A block sits motionless on a rough horizontal floor. Two forces, F₁ (pressing straight down on top of the block) and F₂ (pushing horizontally against the block), act on it at the same time. Raising the value of either force — F₁ or F₂ — will make the friction force on the block larger. Reason: Increasing F₁ makes the ground's normal reaction on the block larger.

options.1: If both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is correct explanation of the Assertion.
options.2: If both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
options.3: If Assertion is true, but the Reason is false.
options.4: If Assertion is false but the Reason is true.

conditions: F₁ acts vertically downward on top of the block
F₂ acts horizontally, pushing the block

figure.description: The block sits on a horizontal rough floor, drawn as a straight ground line. F₁ is drawn as an arrow pointing straight down onto the top of the block. F₂ is drawn as an arrow pointing horizontally to the right, pushing into the block from its left side.

solution.approach: The block stays at rest, so friction must equal the horizontal push F₂ alone; check separately whether raising F₁ or raising F₂ changes that value.

steps.text: The block stays at rest, so along the ground the friction force must exactly balance the horizontal push F₂.
If F₂ increases while F₁ stays fixed, the friction needed for equilibrium increases too, since it must still equal F₂.
If F₁ increases while F₂ stays fixed, the horizontal force to balance is still F₂, so the actual friction in use does not change.

Increasing F₁ only raises the normal reaction and the maximum friction available, μN, not the friction actually being used — so the Assertion's claim that either force increases friction fails for F₁ alone, making the Assertion false.
Taken by itself, the Reason is a true statement: pressing down harder with F₁ does raise the normal reaction from the ground.

final_answer.value: If the Assertion is false but the Reason is true.

common_mistakes.text: Assuming a larger normal reaction by itself always means larger actual friction, missing that it only raises the friction limit, and picking both statements true with the Reason explaining it.
